verdict.rationale: Open WebUI documents programmatic, non-UI access. API keys let external code call the same endpoints the web UI uses. The Computer gateway exposes workspaces as OpenAI-compatible models, so any OpenAI-style client can run agent tasks. There is also a single-command CLI (`cptr run`), and the product deploys via Docker or Kubernetes. However, nothing documents a headless or CI mode as such, and the CLI's purpose is undescribed; built-in scheduled Automations are an in-product recurring schedule, not CI integration. missing for 10: explicit headless/CI usage docs (e.g. CI pipeline examples, non-interactive exit codes), description of what the CLI run command does in automation, independent or hands-on corroboration of CI use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: An API key is a personal access token that lets external code call the same endpoints the web UI uses.
The gateway exposes each of your workspaces as an OpenAI-compatible model, so any OpenAI-style client can run agent tasks in a real workspace.
The CLI has exactly one command: cptr run
Install seamlessly via pip, uv, Docker, or Kubernetes (kubectl, kustomize, or helm)
